headline: Essar Power appoints Soumiya Venkateswaran as head-HR
summary: Essar Power has appointed Soumiya Venkateswaran as its new Head of Human Resources, effective August 2026. She brings over 20 years of strategic HR leadership experience across various sectors, having previously served as Senior Vice President of HR at Axis Bank. In her new role, Venkateswaran will lead workforce planning, talent management, and organizational effectiveness to support Essar Power's growth objectives.

headline: IT hiring takes divergent turns in Q2 as workforce numbers shift
summary: India's top four IT services firms reported divergent workforce trends in Q2, signaling distinct strategic priorities rather than a uniform industry recovery. HCLTech, Infosys, and TCS expanded their employee bases through fresher hiring, falling attrition, and upskilling efforts, while Wipro contracted its headcount by over 6,700 employees. Overall, these contrasting workforce movements reflect varying operational approaches to talent management and efficiency across the sector.

headline: American Express to cut 5% of workforce as it restructures for AI adoption
summary: American Express is cutting approximately 5 percent of its global workforce as part of a restructuring plan to increase efficiency and integrate artificial intelligence into its operations. The move involves flattening management layers and will result in a $336 million charge for the credit card issuer. This decision mirrors a growing trend among financial institutions, including Barclays, adjusting their workforce structures alongside AI investments.

headline: POV: Are organisations mistaking visible passion for genuine commitment?
summary: Business leaders warn that organizations risk mistaking visible enthusiasm and overwork for genuine employee commitment. When going above and beyond becomes a constant expectation, voluntary passion turns into pressure that forces employees to perform dedication for job security. HR experts advise companies to focus on sustainable performance and actual value creation rather than judging loyalty based on outward visibility.

headline: Rupal Rajal to head HR for CheQ
summary: Indian credit card management platform CheQ has appointed XLRI alumna Rupal Rajal as its new Head of Human Resources. Rajal brings extensive HR leadership experience from previous roles at organizations including Accenture, Kerry, Rupifi, and Findem. In her new role, she will focus on embedding HR as a core driver of workforce transformation, leadership development, and organizational capability.

headline: Shram Samvad begins in Lucknow today; to build awareness on Labour Codes and worker welfare
summary: India's Ministry of Labour & Employment and the Uttar Pradesh government have initiated a two-day 'Shram Samvad' workshop in Lucknow to educate employers and HR leaders on the country's four new labour codes. The programme focuses on streamlining compliance, utilizing tech platforms like e-Shram, and expanding social protection for gig and unorganised workers. Part of a 90-day nationwide campaign, the event offers industry stakeholders a direct platform to address operational and regulatory concerns with government officials.

headline: Are IT jobs reviving? Infosys hired 4,480 in Q2
summary: Infosys added 4,480 employees in Q2 FY27, signaling a potential revival in IT hiring despite relatively flat year-over-year headcount growth across the sector. The company brought on 8,000 freshers during the quarter, putting it on track to hit its annual target of 20,000 entry-level hires. This hiring push highlights how tech firms are continuing to invest in early-career talent even as AI tools reshape service delivery models.

headline: Micron introduces global profit-linked bonus plan after union pressure
summary: Following union negotiations in Taiwan, Micron Technology will introduce a global quarterly bonus scheme linked to company profits starting in fiscal 2027. The plan splits payouts evenly between cash and one-year vesting shares, alongside increases to annual incentive caps and enhanced localized benefits for its Taiwanese workforce. The decision reflects broader pressure on semiconductor manufacturers to share AI-driven financial gains with their employees.

headline: Uber rolls out AI training and productivity tools to 30,000 employees
summary: Uber is expanding an AI-powered productivity platform and dedicated training to over 30,000 global employees following a successful 1,000-person pilot. The company-wide deployment integrates with workplace tools like Google Drive and Slack to help staff automate multi-step tasks, conduct research, and analyze data. Uber and partner OpenAI plan to share insights on employee adoption and measurable productivity outcomes as the rollout progresses.

headline: Wingify appoints Sahil Sharma as global CPO
summary: Wingify has appointed Sahil Sharma as its global chief people officer to lead the company's HR priorities, talent acquisition, and organizational development. Sharma joins the software company following a decade-long tenure at RateGain, where he most recently served as group CHRO. In his new role, he will focus on aligning global workforce strategies with Wingify's long-term business growth.

headline: BHEL appoints M Sridhar as director – HR
summary: Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL) has appointed company veteran M Sridhar as Director – Human Resources to its board. Bringing over 36 years of cross-functional experience across manufacturing, commercial operations, and HR at BHEL, Sridhar previously served as Executive Director – HR. In his new role, he will lead the public-sector enterprise's workforce strategy, focusing on policy formulation, performance management, and organizational development.

headline: Indraprastha Gas appoints Ajeet Kumar as chief general manager – HRD
summary: Indraprastha Gas has named Ajeet Kumar as its Chief General Manager of Human Resource Development. Kumar brings over 19 years of HR experience, including nearly 18 years in leadership roles at NTPC spanning talent acquisition, employee relations, and strategic workforce planning. In his new position at IGL, he will oversee the company's people strategy, organizational culture, and talent management functions.

headline: Time OOH elevates Amit Unadkat to vice president
summary: Time OOH has promoted Amit Unadkat to Vice President and National Head of Direct Client Partnership. In his new role, Unadkat will oversee the direct client partnership vertical, drawing on more than 23 years of experience across the telecom, BFSI, and media sectors. Prior to his six-year tenure at Time OOH, he held positions at several major organizations including Zee, Big FM, and Vodafone.

headline: Z appoints Komal Nahta as creative director for movies business
summary: Zee Entertainment Enterprises has appointed veteran film analyst Komal Nahta as creative director for its movies business following a restructuring of its Zee Studios and acquisition verticals. Reporting directly to CEO Punit Goenka, Nahta will lead content evaluation, production, commissioning, and distribution across theatrical, television, and digital platforms. The operational realignment aims to streamline decision-making and combine creative conviction with commercial discipline across Hindi and regional language films.

headline: Wow! Momo Foods to enter Sri Lanka, eyes UAE & US for QSR expansion
summary: Wow! Momo Foods is initiating its international QSR expansion by entering Sri Lanka through a master franchise agreement with Softlogic Corporation, targeting 20 outlets over two years. The company is also evaluating entry into the UAE and plans to launch in the US market within two years. Additionally, its packaged goods arm, Wow! FMCG, already distributes products across 14 countries and more than 1,000 international touchpoints.
